issues.legal_issue: A proposed transferee cannot protect possession of immovable property by part performance unless a written contract states terms from which the transfer can be ascertained with reasonable certainty.
material_facts: The respondents claimed that an oral agreement had been made to sell one co-owner’s half share and that part of the price had been paid.

The co-owner’s letters acknowledged an agreement to sell and demanded payment of the balance, but did not set out essential terms, including when the sale deed was to be executed and who would pay registration charges.
The occupant had originally entered the property permissively, and possession had not been given pursuant to a written agreement containing the terms of the proposed transfer.
issues.conclusion: The letters were not a written agreement to sell satisfying the requirements for protection by part performance. The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s judgment was set aside, and the owners’ suit for possession and mesne profits was decreed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 53-A of the Transfer of Property Act requires a contract to transfer immovable property for consideration, in writing and signed by the transferor or someone on the transferor’s behalf, with terms ascertainable with reasonable certainty; it also requires possession in part performance, an act in furtherance, and performance or willingness to perform by the transferee. The written contract must precede possession claimed under it. The Court relied on Nathulal v. Phool Chand (1969) 3 SCC 120 and Sardar Govindrao Mahadik v. Devi Sahai (1982) 1 SCC 237 for these requirements.

predicates.part_performance_possession_claim: The proceeding includes a claim by a proposed transferee to protect possession of immovable property on the basis of part performance.
predicates.writings_only_acknowledge_oral_sale: The available writings merely acknowledge an oral sale agreement rather than recording its terms as a written contract.
predicates.essential_transfer_terms_absent_from_wri: The writings do not state essential terms needed to ascertain the proposed transfer with reasonable certainty.
predicates.possession_not_given_under_written_contr: The proposed transferee was not put in possession pursuant to a written contract containing the terms of the proposed transfer.

issues.definition: When a proposed transferee seeks to protect possession by part performance, the protection is unavailable if the writings only acknowledge an oral sale, omit essential transfer terms, and possession was not given under a written contract.
